bullets: The newly released “The Ceiling Is Not the Model” study reports that output limits, decoding settings, and the serving stack changed local large language model scores enough to suppress measured capability, reverse a ranking, and create an apparent reasoning loop. Its five-arm design isolates each configuration effect and includes raw records and a triage protocol. Why it matters: If you compare locally served models, this means the evaluation must vary and record token budgets, decoding, and serving settings before attributing score differences to model weights; otherwise, a deployment setting may determine the ranking. Evidence: E047. Medium confidence.

A newly captured medical study tested ten large language models as autonomous judges on three structurally different clinical tasks, with human reference labels and three repeated judgments per case. It reports that performance validated on one task did not remain stable on another. Why it matters: If you use a model to grade medical answers, research appraisals, or triage decisions, validation on one task does not establish suitability for another; each target task needs its own human-referenced judge evaluation. Evidence: E085. High confidence.

The new corpus-assay release scans large language model training collections for benchmark contamination using auditable n-grams—short, exact text fragments—and attributes matches to individual benchmarks and test items. Why it matters: If you are deciding whether benchmark scores reflect generalization rather than memorized test material, this adds an inspection step that can identify exactly which evaluation items overlap a training collection instead of returning only a corpus-level warning. Evidence: E004. Medium confidence.

The new Cross-Dataset Human Activity Recognition Benchmark package compares ten models across five sensor datasets using harmonized accelerometer inputs and five subject-disjoint folds per dataset, meaning the people represented in evaluation folds are separated. It includes scripts, results, provenance, verification tools, and documented limitations. Why it matters: If you are choosing a suite for wearable-sensor generalization, this package supports comparisons across datasets while reducing person-specific leakage and makes the reported results independently rerunnable. Evidence: E002. High confidence.

The new agentic-safety-bench project evaluates whether agent security scanners detect behavior recorded in action logs rather than relying only on what an agent says it did. Why it matters: If you evaluate safeguards for tool-using agents, this changes the ground truth from generated text to executed actions. That can expose scanners that accept safe-sounding responses while missing unsafe tool behavior. Evidence: E031. Medium confidence.

The new Semantic Cache Adversarial Benchmark targets the cache that decides whether to reuse a previous answer. Its cases include poisoned stored answers and one-token changes involving negation, numbers, or entities near the cache’s similarity threshold. Why it matters: If your product reuses answers based on semantic similarity, model-only testing is incomplete. This artifact lets you test whether the caching layer returns a wrong prior answer when a small wording change materially changes the request. Evidence: E006. Medium confidence.

The new Tibetan Translation Benchmark reports modern and religious Tibetan separately and offers a companion balanced ranking that combines the two registers. This preserves information about where a model performs well instead of exposing only one blended score. Why it matters: If you are selecting a Tibetan-to-English model, this means the evaluation can match the intended text register; a combined leaderboard position alone may conceal a model that works for modern text but not classical religious material, or vice versa. Evidence: E007. Medium confidence.
bullets_zh: 新发布的研究“The Ceiling Is Not the Model”报告称，输出限制、解码设置和服务栈对本地大语言模型分数的影响足以压低测得的能力、逆转排名，并制造出表面上的推理循环。其五组实验设计隔离了各项配置的影响，并提供原始记录和分诊协议。Why it matters: 如果你要比较本地部署的大语言模型，就必须在将分数差异归因于模型权重之前，改变并记录 token 预算、解码和服务设置；否则，部署设置可能会决定排名。Evidence: E047. Medium confidence.

一项新收录的医学研究以三种结构不同的临床任务测试了十个大语言模型作为自主评判模型的表现，并采用人工参考标签，且对每个病例重复评判三次。研究报告称，在一项任务上得到验证的表现，在另一项任务上并未保持稳定。Why it matters: 如果你使用模型为医学答案、研究评析或分诊决策评分，那么在一项任务上的验证并不能证明它适用于另一项任务；每项目标任务都需要单独开展以人工参考标签为基准的评判模型评估。Evidence: E085. High confidence.

新发布的语料检测工具使用可审计的 n-gram（即短小且完全匹配的文本片段）扫描大语言模型训练语料集中的基准污染，并将匹配结果归因到具体基准和测试条目。Why it matters: 如果你要判断基准分数反映的是泛化能力还是对测试材料的记忆，该工具增加了一个检查步骤，可以准确识别哪些评估条目与训练语料集重叠，而不是只返回语料库层面的警告。Evidence: E004. Medium confidence.

新发布的 Cross-Dataset Human Activity Recognition Benchmark 工具包使用统一的加速度计输入，在五个传感器数据集上比较十个模型，并对每个数据集采用五个受试者互斥的折叠，也就是说，评估折叠中所代表的人员彼此分离。该工具包包含脚本、结果、数据来源、验证工具和有记录的局限性。Why it matters: 如果你要为可穿戴传感器的泛化评估选择套件，该工具包既支持跨数据集比较，又能减少特定于个人的信息泄漏，并使报告结果可以由第三方独立重新运行。Evidence: E002. High confidence.
新发布的 agentic-safety-bench 项目评估智能体安全扫描器能否检测行动日志中记录的行为，而不是仅依赖智能体声称自己做了什么。Why it matters: 如果你要评估工具调用型智能体的防护措施，这会将真实标签从生成文本转向实际执行的操作。由此可以识别出那些接受听起来安全的回答、却漏检不安全工具行为的扫描器。Evidence: E031. Medium confidence.

新发布的 Semantic Cache Adversarial Benchmark 针对的是决定是否复用先前答案的缓存。其测试用例包括被投毒的已存储答案，以及在缓存相似度阈值附近对否定词、数字或实体进行单个 token 改动的情况。Why it matters: 如果你的产品基于语义相似度复用答案，仅测试模型并不完整。借助该评测产物，你可以测试当措辞上的微小变化实质性改变请求时，缓存层是否会返回错误的先前答案。Evidence: E006. Medium confidence.

新发布的 Tibetan Translation Benchmark 分别报告现代藏文和宗教藏文的表现，并提供一个配套的平衡排名，将这两种语体结合起来。这样可以保留模型擅长领域的信息，而不是只展示一个混合分数。Why it matters: 如果你要选择藏译英模型，这意味着评估可以匹配预期的文本语体；仅看综合排行榜名次，可能会掩盖某个模型适用于现代文本却不适用于古典宗教材料的情况，反之亦然。Evidence: E007. Medium confidence.

evidence_items.summary: Cross-Dataset HAR Benchmark: Verified Reproducibility Package (v1.0.0) This software archive accompanies the research manuscript Cross-Dataset Human Activity Recognition with Time-Series Foundation Models: A Subject-Disjoint Benchmark of Generalization, Robustness, and Efficiency. The benchmark evaluates 10 human activity recognition models across five datasets (WISDM, UCI HAR, MHEALTH, PAMAP2, and MotionSense), using harmonized accelerometer inputs and five subject-disjoint evaluation folds per dataset. The release contains evaluation scripts, benchmark results, reproducibility verification tools, provenance information, and documentation of experimental limitations. The original 250 benchmark evaluations underwent saved-result integrity checks. Additional author-server GPU verification reproduced frozen feature extraction for MOMENT-1, MantisV2, and the CrossHAR SSL encoder, comparing 1,059,116,544 numerical values with exact agreement against retained reference artifacts. These checks establish reproducibility of selected saved-checkpoint computations in the authors' environment. They do not constitute independent clean-environment reproduction or fresh retraining of all models. The archive excludes original raw datasets, pretrained model weights, and private checkpoints. Third-party software remains subject to its original licensing terms. evidence_items.summary: Modern Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit structural limitations that reduce their reliability – such as opaque reasoning processes and limited exploration of alternative solution paths – which prompt engineering techniques such as Chain of Thoughts (CoT) can address only partially. This paper introduces an Agentic Graph of Thoughts (AGoT), which extends the Graph of Thoughts (GoT) prompting technique to an agentic framework. In AGoT, LLM-powered agents leverage a dynamically-constructed graph to record their reasoning, possibly including generation, tool invocation, self-evaluation, and tool-crafting steps. Agents can explore multiple reasoning paths, possibly backtracking and extending the graph as needed, while making their reasoning process more explicit and inspectable. AGoT supports dynamic tool use and crafting: new tools can be autonomously generated at runtime when no available tool can solve the problem. We evaluate our approach on the Hendrycks MATH benchmark, comparing the proposed architecture against a Zero-Shot CoT baseline across three different Gemini models. Results suggest that AGoT can make reasoning more robust, as the multi-path exploration and tool-crafting mechanisms help agents recover from incorrect reasoning steps and address a wider variety of problems. Talk given at 24th International Conference of the Italian Association for Artificial Intelligence, Perugia, Italy, 8 October 2026. Record on APICe: https://talks.apice.unibo.it/AgotAixia2026
evidence_items.title: Agentic Graph of Thoughts (AGoT): A Reasoning Framework for LLM Agents

evidence_items.summary: Overview Problematic smartphone use and internalizing anxiety frequently co-occur in adolescence. Quantifying how extracurricular physical activity buffers this pathway remains difficult because daily movement durations inhabit a closed 24-hour simplex and both exposures share psychosocial confounding. Standard moderated regression and Euclidean dose-response estimators treat exercise volume as a free scalar, ignoring whether added activity displaces sedentary screen time or sleep. We formulate PhyBuff-Net, a compositional counterfactual dose-response network coupled with constrained isotemporal prescription optimization (CIPO), evaluated on a multi-school cohort of N=3,600 adolescents across junior high (n=1,600) and senior high (n=2,000) grades. PhyBuff-Net maps 24-hour movement compositions into orthonormal isometric log-ratio coordinates, decouples joint selection bias via double-continuous Hilbert-Schmidt and contrastive balancing, estimates zero-anchored buffering surfaces via orthogonalized Bernstein splines, and pairs entropic mirror-ascent donor optimization with circadian boundary projection and local effective-sample-size shrinkage. On the held-out test split (N test=720, five seeds) and five-split outer cross-validation under shared-donor evaluation, PhyBuff-Net achieves counterfactual surface determinations of 0.9566± 0.0105 and 0.9421± 0.0103 versus 0.9244± 0.0057 for stratified interaction networks and 0.8930± 0.0162 for contrastive balancing representation learning, lowers policy regret from 2.4729 to 1.8932, and eliminates circadian feasibility violations (0.00%). Quantifying how extracurricular physical activity buffers this pathway remains difficult because daily movement durations inhabit a closed 24-hour simplex and both exposures share psychosocial confounding. Standard moderated regression and Euclidean dose-response estimators treat exercise volume as a free scalar, ignoring whether added activity displaces sedentary screen time or sleep. We formulate PhyBuff-Net, a compositional counterfactual dose-response network coupled with constrained isotemporal prescription optimization (CIPO), evaluated on a multi-school cohort of N=3,600 adolescents across junior high (n=1,600) and senior high (n=2,000) grades. PhyBuff-Net maps 24-hour movement compositions into orthonormal isometric log-ratio coordinates, decouples joint selection bias via double-continuous Hilbert-Schmidt and contrastive balancing, estimates zero-anchored buffering surfaces via orthogonalized Bernstein splines, and pairs entropic mirror-ascent donor optimization with circadian boundary projection and local effective-sample-size shrinkage. On the held-out test split (N_test=720, five seeds) and five-split outer cross-validation under shared-donor evaluation, PhyBuff-Net achieves counterfactual surface determinations of 0.9566± 0.0105 and 0.9421± 0.0103 versus 0.9244± 0.0057 for stratified interaction networks and 0.8930± 0.0162 for contrastive balancing representation learning, lowers policy regret from 2.4729 to 1.8932, and eliminates circadian feasibility violations (0.00%). abstract Counterfactual dose-response estimation, Compositional data analysis, Isotemporal substitution, Smartphone addiction, Adolescent anxiety, Constrained prescription optimization Introductionsec:intro Adolescent smartphone overdependence and internalizing anxiety symptoms reinforce one another through disrupted nocturnal circadian regulation, elevated academic distress, and progressive social withdrawal kwon2013sassv,cao2023anxiety,zhang2025comorbidity. Across secondary school populations, elevated scores on the Smartphone Addiction Scale-Short Version (SAS-SV) consistently track higher scores on the 21-item Depression Anxiety Stress Scales (DASS-21) anxiety subscale. In a multi-grade senior high school cohort facing intensive examination schedules, 50.72% of students met the SAS-SV smartphone addiction criterion ren2022movement,lovibond1995dass,hua2025associations. Extracurricular physical activity (EPA) acts as a modifiable behavioral buffer that attenuates both addictive smartphone engagement and downstream anxious arousal; it is typically indexed on the Physical Activity Rating Scale (PARS, 3-item version PARS-3) or via 24-hour accelerometry huang2026temporal,peng2025abuse,qin2025smartphone. Estimating an individualized dose-response buffering curve from observational school cohorts nevertheless confronts a structural physical constraint aitchison1982simplex,chastin2015coda,dumuid2019isotemporal. Every adolescent's day sums strictly to 1,440 min across sleep (SLP), sedentary behavior (SB), light physical activity (LPA), and moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA). Because 24-hour movement behaviors reside on a closed simplex, increasing extracurricular exercise by 30-60 min/day must draw an equal duration from at least one remaining behavioral compartment egozcue2003ilr,ren2022movement,byun2024screen. Reallocating time from recreational screen-based sedentary behavior into MVPA produces pronounced reductions in somatic and cognitive anxiety zhou2024replacing,hua2025associations. Drawing that same exercise duration from nocturnal sleep, among already sleep-restricted senior high school students, impairs sleep quality and exacerbates anxious distress qin2025smartphone,xiao2024relationship. Classical parametric moderated mediation models collapse this compositional substitution structure into a single linear product term. The standard instance is ordinary least squares (OLS) regression with bilinear interaction terms (PROCESS-OLS) hayes2018process,cao2023anxiety,peng2025abuse, which cannot capture threshold saturation or donor-specific sign reversals. Conversely, linear Compositional Data Analysis (CoDA) isotemporal substitution models respect closure on the Aitchison simplex chastin2015coda,dumuid2019isotemporal but assume homogeneous log-ratio slopes across the entire population, overlooking nonlinear interaction dynamics across mild, moderate, and severe smartphone addiction strata. Recent causal machine learning and continuous dose-response architectures relax parametric functional assumptions for continuous interventions shalit2017estimating,schwab2020drnet,feuerriegel2024causal. They include varying-coefficient neural networks (VCNet) nie2021vcnet, gradient interpolation and kernel smoothing (GIKS) nagalapatti2024giks, and contrastive balancing representation learning (CBRL) zhu2024cbrl. Despite their flexibility on univariate exposures, applying Euclidean dose-response estimators directly to adolescent physical activity and smartphone addiction reveals three methodological failure modes. First, Euclidean networks treat the target EPA dose D_EPA as a free scalar independent of the 24-hour movement vector t_i S^4_1440, ignoring donor-compartment heterogeneity and generating counterfactual allocations whose proportional sleep draws breach physiological sleep floors. Second, smartphone addiction A_i and physical activity dose D_EPA,i are jointly confounded by school adjustment, academic pressure, and family socioeconomic standing kim2022kyrbs,cao2023anxiety,zhou2025pretraining. Single-exposure balancing penalties leave the bivariate exposure distribution P(A, D_EPA x, t) coupled in off-diagonal regions where severe smartphone addiction coincides with high physical activity volume. Third, standard neural estimators issue unguarded point prescriptions without verifying whether a candidate exercise increment is supported by local observational density or executable within an adolescent's mandatory school schedule schweisthal2024reliable. We address these challenges in PhyBuff-Net, a compositional counterfactual dose-response network coupled with Constrained Isotemporal Prescription Optimization (CIPO) across four architectural components (C1-C4). A counterfactual dose must enter the model as a valid 24-hour composition rather than as a free scalar. In component one (C1), an Isometric Compositional Time-Reallocation Encoder (ICTE) maps each movement vector into orthonormal Helmert isometric log-ratio (ilr) coordinates and carries the donor choice through an explicit simplex reallocation. Deconfounding one margin of the exposure pair leaves the other biased, because (A, D_EPA) is selected jointly. In component two (C2), a Double-Continuous Contrastive Kernel Balancing Representation (DC-KBR) learner extends Kernel Balancing Representation (KBR) by penalizing residual dependence between the latent state and both exposures at once. It combines a conditional Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion (HSIC) and quantile-stratified InfoNCE contrastive regularization with stabilized Gaussian-kernel density-ratio balancing weights. In component three (C3), the response surface is estimated through a Varying-Coefficient Orthogonal Buffering Spline (VC-OBS) head built on degree-M Bernstein polynomials with second-order knot smoothness. Unlike an unconstrained neural readout, VC-OBS returns zero-anchored closed-form buffering curves and analytical donor utility gradients. In component four (C4), prescriptions are optimized by the CIPO module over the learned surface. CIPO combines circadian and schedule boundary projection (C4a), entropic mirror-ascent donor optimization (C4b), and local effective sample size (ESS, N_eff) support shrinkage (C4c), driving the circadian Feasibility Violation Rate (FVR) to zero. We evaluate the complete framework on a multi-school cohort of N = 3,600 de-identified adolescents spanning grades 7-12 with 12-week wave-2 longitudinal follow-up. Across the canonical held-out test split (N_test = 720) and five-split shared-donor outer cross-validation, PhyBuff-Net accurately recovers the counterfactual dose-response surface (R^2_CF = 0.9566 ± 0.0105 and 0.9421 ± 0.0103), separates screen-time substitution gains from sleep-displacement rebound, and eliminates circadian feasibility violations (0.00%). Related Worksec:related Adolescent smartphone addiction, anxiety, and physical activity moderationsec:rel_domain Psychometric and epidemiological investigations establish a robust positive association between adolescent smartphone addiction and anxiety severity kwon2013sassv,lovibond1995dass,kim2022kyrbs. In junior high school cohorts, Cao et al. cao2023anxiety demonstrated that smartphone addiction measured via SAS-SV correlates positively with DASS-21 anxiety (r = 0.392) and negatively with school adjustment (r = -0.596). Physical activity measured on PARS-3 moderates and buffers the pathway from internalizing distress to problematic phone use. In a multi-grade senior high school investigation (N = 1,323), Ren et al. ren2022movement reported a 50.72% SAS-SV addiction rate. Within that cohort SAS-SV scores rise monotonically across no-anxiety (30.13 ± 9.03), mild (35.37 ± 8.52), moderate (41.70 ± 10.66), and severe (43.90 ± 13.70) anxiety strata. More recent cross-sectional and longitudinal studies confirm that extracurricular physical exercise mitigates internet and smartphone addiction comorbidity with anxiety peng2025abuse,zhang2025comorbidity,qin2025smartphone,xiao2024relationship. These empirical studies, however, rely on linear regression or Hayes PROCESS macro models hayes2018process that treat physical activity as a categorical moderator or a linear interaction term. Such models cannot estimate minimum effective exercise doses individually across a continuous addiction spectrum. Compositional data analysis on the 24-hour movement simplexsec:rel_coda Daily time-use epidemiology recognizes that sleep, sedentary behavior, light activity, and moderate-to-vigorous activity form a strictly closed composition summing to 1,440 min/day aitchison1982simplex,chastin2015coda. Egozcue et al. egozcue2003ilr introduced the isometric log-ratio (ilr) transformation, which maps simplex vectors onto unconstrained Euclidean coordinates under the Aitchison geometry. Dumuid et al. dumuid2019isotemporal formalized compositional isotemporal substitution, which quantifies health changes when fixed durations (e.g., 15-30 min/day) are reallocated from one movement behavior to another. Applied to student and adolescent health, compositional and isotemporal analyses show that replacing sedentary behavior with MVPA is associated with lower smartphone addiction (ilr_1 = -0.453 in adolescent CoDA ren2022movement) and reduced anxiety symptoms zhou2024replacing,hua2025associations. Insufficient sleep duration and sleep disorders run the other way and exacerbate anxious distress qin2025smartphone,xiao2024relationship. Parallel adolescent isotemporal substitution models likewise quantify screen-time reallocation trade-offs across somatic health markers byun2024screen. Nevertheless, existing compositional substitution methods remain parametric linear models without deconfounded representation learning, counterfactual surface estimation, or individualized donor-allocation optimization. Continuous dose-response and counterfactual representation learningsec:rel_causal Counterfactual representation learning originally addressed binary treatments by minimizing distributional divergence between treated and control covariates shalit2017estimating,wager2018causalforest,chernozhukov2018dml. Cross-fitted Double Machine Learning (DML) similarly orthogonalizes nuisance treatment and outcome regressions chernozhukov2018dml,wager2018causalforest. To handle continuous interventions, DRNet schwab2020drnet discretized dosage into strata, SciGAN bica2020scigan employed adversarial networks, and VCNet nie2021vcnet parameterized the outcome head as a varying-coefficient B-spline of the continuous dose. Subsequent advances introduced normalizing flows and missing-treatment estimators for interventional distributions melnychuk2023normalizing,kuzmanovic2023estimating, consensus-enabled robust counterfactual regression (CE-RCFR) wang2024cercfr, two-stage pretraining-finetuning under confounding zhou2025pretraining, and causal mediation frameworks farbmacher2022mediation,feuerriegel2024causal. Three lines bear most directly on our work. Adaptive spline plug-in estimators target nonparametric causal dose-response curves shi2026hal, and GIKS nagalapatti2024giks leverages gradient interpolation and kernel smoothing to regularize counterfactual derivatives in sparse dosage regions. Continuous-treatment representation learners instead decouple selection bias, through adversarial balancing kazemi2024counterfactual, Hilbert-Schmidt kernel independence gretton2005hsic, or contrastive balancing (CBRL) zhu2024cbrl. Yet none of these architectures respects compositional closure on a 24-hour time simplex or decouples joint selection bias across two interacting continuous exposures under physiological feasibility constraints schweisthal2024reliable. Positivity-constrained off-policy prescription and donor optimizationsec:rel_agent Reliable individualized treatment prescription from observational cohorts requires constraining candidate interventions to regions with sufficient overlap (positivity) and domain-specific physiological feasibility schweisthal2024reliable,feuerriegel2024causal,chernozhukov2018dml. Unconstrained neural predictors emit single-pass point optima that can extrapolate into low-density dosage tails or violate circadian and schedule invariants on the 24-hour time-use simplex dumuid2019isotemporal. Positivity-constrained off-policy optimization instead pairs functional outcome estimation with explicit polytope projection over feasible donor allocations, mirror-ascent optimization on the probability simplex, and local effective-sample-size shrinkage in sparse regions schweisthal2024reliable. In compositional dose-response estimation, coupling constrained isotemporal prescription optimization (CIPO) directly with a learned varying-coefficient surface ensures that every candidate EPA recommendation satisfies circadian sleep floors, mandatory study schedules, and local observational support before prescription selection. All cohort assessments were conducted under institutional ethics approval with written guardian informed consent and student assent, and all records were irreversibly de-identified prior to analysis. For each participant i 1, , N, x_i R^p denotes baseline demographic, academic, and psychosocial covariates cao2023anxiety. Architectural overviewsec:overview The pipeline keeps closure, deconfounding, surface smoothness, and prescription safety as separate concerns, because each fails in a different way when folded into a single unconstrained predictor (Figure fig:arch and Table tab:arch_summary). In C1, the ICTE module transforms the 24-hour movement vector t_i S^4_1440 into orthonormal isometric log-ratio coordinates v_i R^3 and defines the donor-aware simplex reallocation operator T_simplex. A dose query therefore fixes the whole composition rather than only MVPA. In C2, the DC-KBR module maps (x_i, v_i) to a normalized latent state z_i R^32 while penalizing joint dependence with (A_i, D_EPA,i). It also computes stabilized density-ratio sample weights to remove selection bias shared by both exposures. In C3, the VC-OBS head combines a baseline addiction-anxiety surface g_base(z_i, t_i, a) with degree-M dose Bernstein polynomials, symmetric simplex-Bernstein donor polynomials B_Δ(w_i), and Cholesky-orthonormalized ilr-Bernstein compositional shift bases. That tensor-spline parameterization supplies smooth dose derivatives and closed-form donor gradients without hardcoded sleep thresholds. In C4, the CIPO module acts on the causal surface at inference and prescription time. It optimizes donor weights via centered entropic mirror ascent (C4b), projects allocations onto circadian sleep and study floors (C4a), and regularizes low-support dosage queries via local ESS support shrinkage (C4c). figure[!htbp] Fig/Figure_1.pdf Architecture and stage-by-stage data flow of PhyBuff-Net. Experimental Setupsec:setup Multi-cohort dataset and 24-hour movement distributionssec:dataset We evaluate PhyBuff-Net and all competing estimators on a de-identified multi-school longitudinal adolescent 24-hour movement and mental-health cohort comprising N = 3,600 participants across two developmental stages cao2023anxiety,ren2022movement,kim2022kyrbs. The Junior High School cohort comprises n = 1,600 students across grades 7-9 (553 in G7, 535 in G8, and 512 in G9; mean ± standard deviation (SD) age 13.82 ± 0.97 years, 46.25% male). The Senior High School cohort comprises n = 2,000 students across grades 10-12 (836 in G10, 756 in G11, and 408 in G12; mean age 16.25 ± 0.90 years, 43.60% male). All data collection procedures received institutional ethics approval and written guardian informed consent alongside student assent prior to enrollment. Across participating schools, baseline assessments combined seven-day 24-hour wrist-actigraphy and daily time-use logs with standardized classroom psychometric administrations of the 10-item SAS-SV kwon2013sassv, the 3-item PARS-3 huang2026temporal, and the DASS-21 anxiety subscale lovibond1995dass. A longitudinal wave-2 follow-up assessment was conducted 11-13 weeks later across all N = 3,600 analytic participants (cohort_followup_wave2.csv), recording follow-up exercise doses, 24-hour movement compositions, and DASS-21 anxiety scores. From the initial enrollment pool of 3,933 students (1,794 junior high and 2,139 senior high), standardized quality-control screening excluded 333 candidates due to valid 24-hour actigraphy wear time below 16 h/day (n = 175), incomplete psychometric scale items (n = 108), or failed attention verification checks (n = 50). The resulting cohort-specific admissibility attrition rates are 10.81% in junior high school (11.24% in G7, 10.54% in G8, and 10.65% in G9) and 6.50% in senior high school (6.49% in G10, 6.55% in G11, and 6.42% in G12; Supplementary Table S1). To evaluate individualized counterfactual dose-response estimation and donor-specific time reallocation across the full exposure domain, longitudinal baseline and wave-2 trajectories are paired with pre-computed multi-wave reference dose-response lookup grids (dr_surface_grid.csv and cohort_reference_surface.csv). These reference surfaces index expected anxiety outcomes across PARS-3 doses 0, 5, , 100 and donor allocations w Δ^2 bounded smoothly onto the continuous [0, 42] DASS-21 scale. Stratified block allocation across school cohort, biological sex, baseline SAS-SV risk tier, and circadian sleep status partitions the N = 3,600 analytic cohort into training (n_train = 2,340, 65%), validation (n_val = 540, 15%), and held-out test (n_test = 720, 20%; 320 junior high and 400 senior high) splits. figure[!htbp] Fig/Figure_2.pdf Multi-cohort 24-hour movement composition and empirical correlation structure across N = 3,600 adolescents. All models are trained exclusively on observed baseline tuples (x_i, t_i, A_i, D_EPA,i, Y_i). To ensure strict donor fairness across compositional and Euclidean estimators, counterfactual surface recovery and prescription decision quality are evaluated under a unified shared-donor protocol. Every estimator is scored on the same test grid G_d = 0, 20, 40, 60, 80 (N_test = 720, five seeds s 101, 202, 303, 404, 505, Table tab:main) and across outer cross-validation, cross-cohort, and wave-2 follow-up regimes (Table tab:misspec). Specifically, all counterfactual grids μ_i(A_i, d) are evaluated under the identical canonical shared donor trajectory w^*_i(d) = (w^*_i,SB(d), , 1 - w^*_i,SB(d), , 0)^, where w^*_i,SB(d) = (1, , (0, (t_i,SB - 180)/(0.68,d, 10^-6))) for d > 0 and w^*_i(0) = (1, 0, 0)^. C4b donor steering remains disabled during grid scoring. Downstream prescription optimization is then evaluated via each estimator's recommended intervention (d^*_i, w_i), while the donor-planning ablations (w/o C4b and w/o C4 in Table tab:ablation) additionally evaluate unassisted proportional-donor grids to isolate the surface contribution of C4b mirror ascent. For any evaluated set S 1, , N_test, the primary surface metric is the counterfactual coefficient of determination (R^2_CF, higher is better), paired with the square root of the mean integrated squared error (MISE, denoted MISE, lower is better): align R^2_CF &= 1 - _i S _d G_d (μ_i(A_i, d; w^*_i(d)) - μ_i(A_i, d))^2_i S _d G_d (μ_i(A_i, d; w^*_i(d)) - μ_S)^2, eq:metrics_r2 MISE &= 1|S| , |G_d| _i S _d G_d (μ_i(A_i, d; w^*_i(d)) - μ_i(A_i, d))^2, eq:metrics_mise align Above, μ_S denotes the reference mean across S. We also quantify accuracy on the marginal buffering effect at high intervention intensity (d = 60) and decision quality under each estimator's recommended prescription (d^*_i, w_i). Specifically, we report the root Precision in Estimation of Heterogeneous Effects (PEHE) for buffering (PEHE_buf, lower is better) and the counterfactual policy regret (Regret_feas, lower is better). We also record the circadian and schedule Feasibility Violation Rate (FVR, %, lower is better). align PEHE_buf &= 1|S|_i S(τ_buf,i(A_i, 60; w^*_i(60)) - τ_buf,i(A_i, 60))^2, eq:metrics_pehe Regret_feas &= 1|S|_i S (0, , μ_i(A_i, d^*_i; w_i) - μ_i(A_i, d^*_i; w^*_i(d^*_i))). eq:metrics_regret align Competing baselines and ablation variantssec:baselines The eight competitors span classical moderated regression, compositional time-use analysis, cross-fitted double machine learning, and neural continuous dose-response representation learners: enumerate PROCESS-OLS hayes2018process,cao2023anxiety: Moderated linear regression with main effects (A_i, D_EPA,i), bilinear interaction A_i × D_EPA,i, and full covariate/movement adjustment (x_i, t_i,1:3), trained on all n_train rows via mini-batch Adam ridge optimization. CoDA-Isotemporal chastin2015coda,dumuid2019isotemporal,ren2022movement: Compositional linear moderation on orthonormal ilr coordinates (ilr_1, ilr_2, ilr_3) paired with static one-for-one sedentary-to-MVPA substitution on S^4_1440. CausalForest-DML wager2018causalforest,chernozhukov2018dml: Two-fold cross-fitted double machine learning with bagged variance-reducing regression trees of tuned depth and leaf size, estimating heterogeneous moderated treatment slopes. TARNet-Int shalit2017estimating,schwab2020drnet: Two-layer residual representation network with K = 3 discrete PARS-3 clinical dose-stratum heads ([0, 19], (19, 42], (42, 100]) and within-stratum addiction interaction layers. Backbone-ConcatMLP (No C1-C4): Unconstrained two-layer ReLU multilayer perceptron concatenating (x_i, t_i/1440, A_i, D_EPA,i) without C1, C2, C3, or C4. VCNet nie2021vcnet: Two-layer residual encoder coupled with a degree-3 cubic varying-coefficient truncated-power B-spline head, a four-bin conditional treatment density head, and functional targeted regularization. GIKS nagalapatti2024giks: Two-layer residual encoder and cubic varying-coefficient spline head regularized by local Gaussian kernel dose-gradient interpolation and smoothing. CBRL zhu2024cbrl: Single-treatment contrastive balancing representation learner combining a two-layer residual encoder, continuous treatment HSIC, four-quantile InfoNCE, and Nystr"om marginal density-ratio weights on D_EPA,i while conditioning on A_i as an observed covariate in its cubic spline head. enumerate Baseline feasibility violation rates and policy regret must not reflect unnormalized wrapper drift. All seven non-compositional baselines (methods 1 and 3-8) therefore predict counterfactual non-MVPA contractions via four training-fitted generalized cross-validation (GCV) log-duration ridge regressions projected directly onto the closed 1,440 min/day simplex (0.000 min/day closure error). Section sec:res_error additionally evaluates a feasibility-filtered control (CBRL + C4a) that grants C4a boundary projection directly to CBRL at prescription time, alongside two structural-prior neural control arms (CBRL + StructPrior and VCNet + StructPrior) that receive the same compositional ilr coordinates, empirical training sleep quantiles, and shared donor features as PhyBuff-Net. Nine ablation variants isolate each module on the five-seed protocol. Four variants ablate CIPO by removing C4a (w/o C4a), C4b (w/o C4b), C4c (w/o C4c), or the full CIPO module (w/o C4). Three further variants replace bivariate balancing with marginal balancing (w/o C2-Contrastive), no balancing (w/o C2), or a generic MLP head (w/o C3). The final two replace ICTE and T_simplex with unprojected Euclidean durations (w/o C1) or remove C1-C4 together (w/o C1-C4). Statistical analysis and implementation protocolsec:stat_protocol Every competing baseline and PhyBuff-Net receives identical splits, identical feature access, and a matched hyperparameter search budget of 48 distinct trials fitted on the training split (n_train = 2,340) and evaluated strictly on the validation split (n_val = 540, Supplementary Note 2 and Table tab:tuning). Linear and compositional models evaluate 48 combinations of ridge penalties α [10^-3, 10] and learning rates [0.010, 0.060]. CausalForest-DML samples 48 configurations without replacement over ensemble size, tree depth d_ 2, 3, 4, minimum leaf size n_leaf 15, 25, 40, and DML ridge penalties. All five neural baselines sample 48 configurations without replacement over hidden widths 16, 24, 32, 48, learning rates 0.015, 0.022, 0.030, encoder L_2 weight decays 10^-3, 10^-2, 0.05, 0.15, 0.35, and head/auxiliary regularization weights, ranked by density-ratio-weighted observational validation mean squared error (MSE). PhyBuff-Net samples 48 configurations uniformly without replacement from the 162-point Cartesian grid spanning d_z 24, 32, 48, M 4, 6, 8, λ_bal 0.05, 0.10, 0.18, 0.25, 0.35, 0.50, and τ_nce 0.12, 0.15, 0.20 (evaluate_all.py). Configurations are ranked via the target-free observational validation objective J_val combining density-ratio-weighted factual validation MSE, validation joint exposure HSIC_val, and sample-weight variance regularization, selecting d_z = 32, M = 6, λ_bal = 0.25, and τ_nce = 0.15 (J_val = 3.2253). The inference-time CIPO thresholds τ_ess = 50 and K_ref = 8 are fixed a priori from kernel support and mirror-ascent convergence criteria and audited post-hoc across one-dimensional sensitivity sweeps (Tables tab:sensitivity-tab:sens_harness). Relative to the continuous dose-response neural baselines GIKS (0.8996 ± 0.0099), CBRL (0.8930 ± 0.0162, 95% CI [0.8745, 0.9091]), and VCNet (0.8890 ± 0.0082), PhyBuff-Net improves R^2_CF by +0.0570 (p_Holm = 1.97 × 10^-69), +0.0636 (p_Holm = 6.04 × 10^-52), and +0.0677 (p_Holm = 6.79 × 10^-51), respectively. Compared with CausalForest-DML (0.8855 ± 0.0089), PROCESS-OLS (0.8489 ± 0.0017), Backbone-ConcatMLP (0.8343 ± 0.0078), and CoDA-Isotemporal (0.8097 ± 0.0012), the surface determination gains reach +0.0711 (p_Holm = 6.21 × 10^-78), +0.1077 (p_Holm = 6.83 × 10^-89), +0.1224 (p_Holm = 3.47 × 10^-108), and +0.1470 (p_Holm = 8.92 × 10^-77). 2.6858 & 3.7532 & 1.9195 tabular* table Discussionsec:discussion Two modeling requirements collide in compositional dose-response estimation. Estimating how extracurricular physical activity buffers the pathway from adolescent smartphone addiction to anxiety requires reconciling continuous causal representation learning with the compositional geometry of the 24-hour day. Across our multi-school cohort of N = 3,600 adolescents spanning junior and senior high school grades, standard moderated regressions and donor-agnostic neural estimators systematically misestimate the counterfactual response surface whenever exercise volume is treated as an unconstrained Euclidean scalar. Potential anxiety outcomes depend on a three-way interaction among baseline smartphone addiction severity (A_i), continuous exercise dose (D_EPA,i), and the donor movement compartment (w_i). Under screen-time substitution, adolescents in moderate and severe SAS-SV strata exhibit counterfactual anxiety reductions of 3.33-4.12 DASS-21 points across d [40, 80] zhou2024replacing. Conversely, when high exercise volumes are drawn from nocturnal sleep among sleep-restricted students without circadian boundary projection, sleep depletion erodes the psychological benefit once post-reallocation sleep drops below 420 min/day ren2022movement,hua2025associations,xiao2024relationship. Each architectural module addresses a distinct source of estimation or prescription bias (Tables tab:ablation-tab:misspec). The ICTE module (C1) embeds the 24-hour simplex S^4_1440 directly into orthonormal ilr coordinates and couples every counterfactual dose query to the donor reallocation operator T_simplex. Without C1, unprojected Euclidean log-duration regressions incur 2.000 min/day simplex closure drift (92.92% FVR and 3.1728 policy regret in w/o C1, degrading R^2_CF by -0.0737). DC-KBR (C2) extends continuous treatment balancing from univariate propensity matching nie2021vcnet,zhu2024cbrl to bivariate kernel, contrastive, and stabilized density-ratio balancing over (A_i, D_EPA,i), lowering off-diagonal severe-addiction RMSE from 2.9449 (w/o C2) and 4.8127 (CBRL) to 2.7378 (Table tab:failure). The VC-OBS Bernstein head (C3) keeps the estimated surface zero-anchored and smooth via second-order knot regularization, avoiding the -0.1504 R^2_CF degradation of an unconstrained MLP head. Finally, CIPO (C4) acts on the learned surface at prescription time, cutting policy regret from 3.2848 (w/o C4, 10.14% FVR) to 1.8932 (0.00% FVR) through C4b mirror-ascent donor optimization (Δ R^2_CF = +0.0512 over w/o C4b), C4a circadian boundary projection (eliminating the 8.22% violations of w/o C4a), and C4c local-ESS support regularization. Several methodological and empirical limitations bound the scope of these findings. First, although multi-wave longitudinal follow-up across baseline and 12-week wave-2 assessments anchors the reference dose-response lookup grids and supports out-of-wave validation (RMSE_fact = 1.8656), observational school cohorts remain subject to unmeasured confounding from genetic, familial, or classroom-level shocks; randomized isotemporal substitution trials are needed before translating estimated dose thresholds into clinical guidelines. Second, our compositional encoder partitions the 24-hour day into four aggregate compartments (SLP, SB, LPA, MVPA). Disaggregating sedentary behavior into recreational smartphone screen time versus mandatory classroom and homework seated time via objective mobile-sensing logs would further sharpen the donor-allocation optimizer (C4b). Third, extending CIPO to multi-week ecological momentary assessment wrist-actigraphy cohorts will be essential for prospective validation of dynamic, day-by-day exercise reallocation policies wang2024cercfr,zhou2025pretraining. Conclusionsec:conclusion PhyBuff-Net unifies isometric log-ratio compositional encoding, double-continuous contrastive kernel balancing, varying-coefficient orthogonal Bernstein splines, and constrained isotemporal prescription optimization into a coherent framework for compositional counterfactual dose-response learning. Evaluated across a multi-school adolescent cohort (N = 3,600; held-out N_test = 720 across five seeds), five-split outer cross-validation, and 12-week wave-2 longitudinal follow-up under shared-donor scoring, PhyBuff-Net achieves a counterfactual surface R^2_CF of 0.9566 ± 0.0105 on the canonical test split and 0.9421 ± 0.0103 across outer cross-validation. It reduces surface MISE to 1.6701 ± 0.2034, buffering PEHE_buf to 1.9369 ± 0.2670, and counterfactual policy regret to 1.8932 ± 0.4178 while maintaining a 0.00% circadian feasibility violation rate. Respecting 24-hour compositional closure and circadian sleep boundaries is therefore essential for reliable counterfactual dose-response estimation and safe behavioral prescription optimization. evidence_items.summary: Dataset comprising 116 peer-reviewed articles analysed in a study on the use of bibliometric indicators in science policy and research evaluation. The original corpus of 73 articles was expanded through a retrospective reassessment of the initial Scopus search results, incorporating 43 additional studies. The dataset includes descriptive and analytical variables covering study objectives, relationships with science and technology policy (STP), bibliometric indicators, main findings, conclusions, author affiliation countries, geographic scope, data sources, document types and temporal coverage. It also includes context-specific families of study objectives and a classification into four analytical systems: Descriptive, Evaluative, Structural/Analytical and Strategic/Normative. Bibliometric indicators are classified into four non-mutually exclusive dimensions — Production, Impact, Relational and Thematic — distinguishing indicators applied, mentioned without application, absent or undetermined. The original analytical summaries of the 73 articles were preserved, while summaries for 42 additional full-text articles were prepared with AI assistance and reviewed by the authors. One article, available only as an abstract, remains unclassified in analyses requiring full-text examination. The dataset includes a data dictionary documenting the variables, classification criteria and coding conventions. The articles were retrieved through a Scopus search combining "science policy" with bibliometric and scientometric terms, followed by a retrospective reassessment of the original search results.

evidence_items.summary: With the rapid development of Large Language Models (LLMs), a large number of evaluation benchmarks have been proposed. However, most benchmarks lack unified evaluation standards, requiring users to manually implement customized scripts, which leads to high usage costs and difficulties in ensuring the consistency of evaluation results. Existing evaluation frameworks are typically centralized, integrating scripts, datasets, and reference answers into a single system, which not only increases system complexity but also raises the risk of benchmark leakage. To address these issues, we propose the Decentralized Evaluation Protocol (DEP), which decouples users, LLMs, and benchmarks. By associating each benchmark with a server script that can either be locally mounted or remotely deployed, DEP enables lightweight, plug-and-play, broadly compatible evaluations while preventing data leakage. Once adapted, the benchmark can be reused over the long term. To facilitate practical adoption, we developed the DEP Toolkit, a toolkit compatible with the DEP protocol that supports features such as resumable evaluation, concurrent requests, and congestion control, while also providing both a CLI and a GUI. In addition, we provide detailed documentation to guide benchmark adaptation for DEP. Using the DEP Toolkit, we validated the effectiveness of DEP in applications, demonstrating its ability to reduce the deployment cost of benchmark evaluation. As of May 2026, we have adapted more than 60 benchmarks and continue to promote community-driven collaboration to support unified evaluation across domains.
evidence_items.title: DEP: A Decentralized Evaluation Protocol and Toolkit for Large Language Models

evidence_items.summary: We present a fully automated, end-to-end pipeline for the large-scale multi-label classification of web documents. Our approach addresses the challenge of creating production-ready classifiers without manual annotation while maintaining high classification accuracy. The pipeline combines generative and discriminative ML techniques to construct training datasets and train classifiers without human labeling. A two-stage annotation process generates the training data: semantic dense retrieval pre-selects candidate documents for each category, followed by an LLM-as-a-judge filtering step that achieves near-human annotation quality. A classification model is then trained using the task-specific fine-tuning of a semantic sentence transformer with an MLP head. We evaluate the approach by benchmarking it against the previous production baseline. Each classified pageview contributes to the aggregation of user interests aligned with the IAB Content Taxonomy. These aggregated interests enable the construction of audience segments for advertising applications and serve as features for a downstream ad ranking model. An online A/B test evaluating these system upgrades demonstrates statistically significant improvements in key business metrics (+2.73% CTR).
evidence_items.title: LLM-Powered Pipeline for Web Page Classification

evidence_items.summary: High Energy Saver v2.1 is a prototype-oriented intelligent energy monitoring, control, and optimization platform designed for corporate environments. It simulates telemetry-driven infrastructure management in a centralized dashboard where electrical points are modeled as dynamic nodes distributed across multiple organizational levels (e.g., zones, departments, or building sections). The platform demonstrates how node-level monitoring and control can be used to identify consumption behavior, apply operational shutdown strategies, and estimate the impact of those actions through interactive Statistics Core capabilities in v2.0 Real-time node-grid monitoring and telemetry simulation Manual ON/OFF control and slot-based repeatable actions Scheduler-compatible control logic for operational testing Active/inactive and level-based filtering KPI cards and time-based analytics (Day/Week/Month/Year) Date-range bounded analysis and CSV export UK-DALE dataset replay mode for realistic load-pattern experimentation Analytics model The analytics environment separates telemetry behavior into: Energy Consumed: nodes ON and active Energy Saved: estimated avoided consumption when baseline load is present but nodes are forced OFF This enables evaluation of control impact in a reproducible prototype setting. Research scope High Energy Saver v2.1 is a research software prototype for controlled experimentation and proof-of-concept validation. It does not claim utility-grade metering accuracy or compliance-grade billing use at this stage. Its role is to support intelligent energy decision workflows and prepare for future expert-supervised calibration and monitored real-world deployment.

evidence_items.summary: This dataset provides geometry files, archived OpenFOAM simulation data, reduced-order model inputs, and reproducible analysis code for Gyroid, Diamond, and Primitive sheet-based triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) heat sinks. Original STL geometries are accompanied by calibration records, material properties, boundary conditions, solver dictionaries, convergence logs, and three-dimensional velocity, temperature, and pressure snapshots. A Python workflow regenerates the nine-point Level-1 engineering statistics, evaluates matched-hydraulic-power heat-removal correlations, replays selected spatial-grading designs, and checks calculated results against archived references. The collection includes a uniform Diamond geometry prepared for AlSi10Mg additive manufacturing and its geometric screening records. At 50% solid fraction, fitted correlations favor Diamond at two reference hydraulic powers, but this ranking does not hold uniformly across density. Fine-grid cell-size grading produces predicted thermal-resistance reductions of approximately 1.67–2.41%, below the study-selected 3% threshold. Failed explicit conjugate-heat-transfer energy-balance evidence is retained separately from accepted performance results. No experimental thermal measurement series was recovered; fabrication records are not presented as thermal validation. This supplementary data and code contribution supports inspection, reproduction, and extension of the computational study associated with an ICEESE submission. It is not a duplicate paper or a claim of IEEE scientific peer review.

evidence_items.summary: This research dataset presents a comprehensive collection of experimental benchmark results for the Minimum s-Club Cover (MSCC) problem, an NP-hard combinatorial optimization problem in graph theory. The dataset covers 30 benchmark graphs, including 12 real-world complex networks and 18 DIMACS benchmark graphs. It contains experimental results from eight optimization algorithms evaluated using 20 independent paired random seeds, resulting in a total of 4,800 experimental runs. The primary objective is to evaluate the feasibility and performance of integrating Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) into evolutionary algorithms through the PPO-based Adaptive Operator Selection (PPO-AOS) framework combined with a Grouping Genetic Algorithm (GGA). The dataset provides experimental measurements, algorithmic comparisons, solution feasibility assessments, runtime analysis, statistical evaluations, and random seed sensitivity analysis. The evaluation includes Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, Cliff's Delta effect sizes, and statistical power analysis. All reported solutions are independently validated against the s-club diameter constraints. The experimental results demonstrate a 100% feasibility rate across the evaluated benchmark instances. This dataset is intended to support independent verification, reproducibility, comparative algorithm evaluation, and further research in graph-based combinatorial optimization and reinforcement learning. The accompanying data files and research materials are organized to facilitate transparent access, reuse, and independent analysis by the scientific community.
evidence_items.title: A Comprehensive Empirical Benchmark Dataset and Feasibility Assessment of Deep Reinforcement Learning for the Minimum s-Club Cover Problem

evidence_items.summary: Emotion detection represents a vital frontier at the inter-section of affective computing, artificial intelligence, and human-computer interaction (HCI). While traditional uni-modal systems—relying solely on text, speech acoustics, or static facial photographs—have established founda-tional benchmarks, they remain fundamentally fragile in real-world conversational dialogues characterized by lex-ical ambiguity, acoustic sarcasm, and visual occlusions. In this paper, we propose an end-to-end, publication-grade deep learning architecture for Multimodal Emo-tion Detection in Distributed Big Data Streams. Our framework synchronizes three specialized foundation models: a linguistic contextual transformer (RoBERTa-Large), a self-supervised acoustic representation encoder (Wav2Vec 2.0), and a spatiotemporal Vision Transformer (ViT-B/16) integrated with Facial Action Unit (FAU) tracking. To resolve temporal granularity discrepancies and inter-modal information imbalance, we formulate a novel Hierarchical Cross-Modal Attention Fusion (HCAF) network. The HCAF module leverages bidirec-tional multi-head cross-attention to project acoustic and vi-sual features into the linguistic latent subspace, selectively attending to emotional cues across communicative chan-nels. To address severe affective class skew (where neutral utterances dominate dialogue corpora), we design a hy-brid multi-task loss combining Focal Loss (γ = 2.0) with Concordance Correlation Coefficient (CCC) optimization for continuous Valence-Arousal dimensional estimation. Furthermore, we architect a distributed stream ingestion pipeline capable of sustaining over 450 concurrent mul-timodal streams per GPU node with sub-50ms latency, incorporating biometric facial landmark de-identification and vocal tract perturbation to guarantee user privacy under GDPR Article 9.
evidence_items.title: Multimodal Emotion Detection in Distributed Data Streams: Deep Transformer Ensembles, Cross-Modal Attention Fusion, and Benchmark Evaluation

evidence_items.summary: Intrusion detection systems are increasingly paired with eXplainable AI (XAI) so that security analysts can understand and act on machine learning and deep learning model decisions. The explanations themselves, however, may be fragile: a perturbed input can change not only the predicted label but also the feature-importance narrative that justifies it. This paper presents a systematic evaluation of how two gradient-based untargeted evasion attacks, the fast gradient sign method and projected gradient descent (PGD), affect three widely used explainers in intrusion and malware detection: DALEX for dataset-level global importance, SHAP at both global and local granularity, and Integrated Gradients (IG) for local attribution. We quantify explanation stability with three complementary measures, Top-k feature overlap, cosine similarity between attribution vectors, and \documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$L_1$$\end{document} attribution distance, computed over the full test set rather than on individually selected samples. We further separate two effects that are commonly conflated; explanation drift is reported separately for adversarial inputs whose predicted label changes and for those whose predicted label is preserved, which isolates explanation instability from prediction instability. Experiments on CICMalMem22 (obfuscated malware memory forensics) and CICIDS17 (network intrusion) show measurable but method- and dataset-dependent drift when predictions are preserved; the mean Top-5 overlap ranges from 0.586 to 0.892, while cosine similarity ranges from 0.875 to 0.962. The strongest preserved-prediction drift occurs for SHAP on CICMalMem22 under untargeted PGD. These findings indicate that XAI constitutes an additional attack surface in cybersecurity pipelines and that evaluating an IDS should include explanation-robustness measures alongside accuracy and F1-score.
evidence_items.title: Evaluating the robustness of explainable AI methods to adversarial attacks in intrusion and malware detection

evidence_items.summary: There is a challenge in designing training programmes to balance exercise intensity and the prevention of injury, especially when using exercises like Chinese Tai Chi for both physical conditioning and injury prevention. The research proposes a multi-objective optimization framework which aims to systematically identify optimal training strategies by maximizing training effectiveness while simultaneously minimizing injury risk. Balanced Intensity Optimization for Training with Injury Control using Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm-II (BIOTIC-NSGA), a multi-objective optimization method that aims at maximizing training efficacy and reducing the time spent on injury risk by intelligent training schedule adaptation. The framework was validated using a Tai Chi exercise dataset collected from 16 participants, comprising biomechanical and neuromuscular variables including muscle strength, joint torque, joint angle, activity level, and injury risk to identify personalized training intensities and recovery windows. BIOTIC-NSGA employs the NSGA-II evolutionary algorithm with constraint-dominance logic and repair mapping projection to ensure feasibility in the solution space. The optimization targets minimizing injury probability while maximizing performance and load balance, providing Pareto-optimal scheduling and intensity strategies. Experimental evaluation against benchmark methods using Precision and F1-score metrics demonstrates that BIOTIC-NSGA achieves 9.14% higher Precision and 10.13% higher F1-score, indicating improved training adaptation and injury-risk optimization. The proposed framework provides a data-driven decision-support tool for coaches to optimize Tai Chi training by systematically balancing performance improvement and injury prevention, while its applicability to other exercise domains will be investigated in future work.
evidence_items.title: Balancing strategy between exercise training intensity and injury risk under multi-objective optimization framework

evidence_items.summary: Abstract In this paper, we introduce ScenePilot-4K, a large-scale first-person dataset for safety-aware vision-language learning and evaluation in autonomous driving. Built from public online driving videos, ScenePilot-4K contains 3,847 hours of video and 27.7M front-view frames spanning 63 countries/regions and 1,210 cities. It jointly provides scene-level natural-language descriptions, risk assessment labels, key-participant annotations, ego trajectories, and camera parameters through a unified multi-stage annotation pipeline. Building on this dataset, we establish ScenePilot-Bench, a standardized benchmark that evaluates vision-language models along four complementary axes: scene understanding, spatial perception, motion planning, and GPT-based semantic alignment. The benchmark includes fine-grained metrics and geographic generalization settings that expose model robustness under cross-region and cross-traffic domain shifts. Baseline results on representative open-source and proprietary vision-language models show that current models remain competitive in high-level scene semantics but still exhibit substantial limitations in geometry-aware perception and planning-oriented reasoning. Beyond the released dataset itself, the proposed annotation pipeline serves as a reusable and extensible recipe for scalable dataset construction from public Internet driving videos.

evidence_items.summary: This record accompanies the paper “CHELATE: High precision structure prediction for metalloproteins”. CHELATE is a machine-learning post-docking filter that predicts how far a docked pose places a ligand’s metal-binding group from its crystallographic position, and discards the poses it judges unreliable. The archive contains everything needed to reproduce the results: a snapshot of the analysis code (also at https://github.com/duartegroup/CHELATE, MIT licence); the curated metalloprotein–ligand dataset derived from PLINDER, covering 51,568 protein–ligand systems from 18,406 structures and more than 20 metal ions; all docking inputs and poses for the training, validation and test sets from AutoDock Vina, smina and GNINA, together with the outputs of AutoDock GPU, GPDOCK and MetalloDock; the per-pose feature tables and the trained CHELATE models; the complete evaluation tables; the metal-identity probe inputs; and the coordinates behind the case studies in Figure 4. Provenance records (file hashes, prepared receptors, docking seeds and re-run comparisons) are included, along with a MANIFEST.tsv listing a SHA-256 checksum for every file. The data are released under CC BY 4.0; the code they contain is MIT-licensed.

evidence_items.summary: This public benchmark dataset provides a comprehensive empirical evaluation suite, graph topological metrics, and feasibility assessment records for the Minimum s-Club Cover (MSCC) problem, focusing on the NP-hard, non-hereditary case of s = 2. The dataset encompasses 30 standardized benchmark graphs across two distinct domains: 12 real-world complex networks (spanning social, biological protein-protein interaction, metabolic, and collaboration networks) and 18 symmetric DIMACS benchmark challenge graphs. The experimental records capture 240 benchmark configurations across 8 diverse algorithms evaluated over 20 strictly paired random seeds (yielding 4,800 complete independent runs). Algorithms evaluated include the adaptive Deep Reinforcement Learning framework (PPO-AOS) integrated with a Grouping Genetic Algorithm (GGA), five evolutionary baseline variants (MAB-AOS, Greedy-AOS, No-RL, Fixed-parameter, and Random-operator selection), and two classical constructive heuristics (I-MSM and CCA). All published solutions strictly guarantee 100% feasibility under the diameter constraint, verified via all-pairs shortest paths. The dataset features complete Best Seed Analyses, convergence logs, and non-parametric Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Holm-Bonferroni corrections under an a priori statistical power exceeding 0.85. This open data repository strictly complies with the FAIR data principles to serve as a reproducible baseline for graph combinatorial optimization and machine learning research. (2026-11-04)

evidence_items.summary: This analysis examines how reference composition shapes the interpretation of truthfulness benchmarks used in international language model evaluation. A descriptive cross-sectional analysis uses 6,202 reference answers nested within 817 questions across 38 categories from the 2021. Counts, correctness proportions and answer length distributions are compared using pooled weighting, equal question weighting and contrasts within questions. Adversarial questions contain a higher correct reference proportion, but the difference decreases from 4.80 to 3.35 percentage points when questions receive equal weight. Category proportions range from 21.59 to 60.71 percent. Correct references average 0.99 words longer than incorrect references, while the average contrast within questions is 0.73 words. Opposing patterns across questions and categories qualify this aggregate tendency. Unequal reference enumeration changes descriptive magnitudes by changing each question’s contribution to pooled summaries. The analysis refines benchmark validity by distinguishing reference composition from evaluated capability. Benchmark maintainers and evaluation teams should disclose question denominators, category coverage and weighting conventions to support transparent interpretation across institutional settings.
evidence_items.title: ASSESSING ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN BENCHMARK ITEM CHARACTERISTICS AND REFERENCE ANSWER CORRECTNESS IN LANGUAGE MODEL TRUTHFULNESS EVALUATION

evidence_items.summary: This poster presents the Synthetic Deformable Tubular Benchmark (SDTB), a synthetic dataset for evaluating deformable 3D reconstruction. The dataset comprises six tubular geometry families and 5,580 RGB images, linked to ground-truth geometry, material point identities, and mechanical data. These references enable tracking individual surface points over time and comparing estimated displacements against known motion. As a demonstration, we evaluate displacement field interpolation from 56 noisy 3D observations using the provided geometry and correspondences. In the reported experiments, finite element method (FEM) regularization reduces interpolation error by approximately 19% for FEM-compatible displacement fields but increases it by approximately 24% for non-FEM fields, relative to radial basis function (RBF) interpolation. The poster highlights both the potential benefits and limitations of physics-based regularization under controlled synthetic conditions. Links to the dataset, reproducibility materials, and accompanying preprint are provided through QR codes.
evidence_items.title: Synthetic Deformable Tubular Benchmark: A Dataset for Evaluating Deformable 3D Reconstruction

evidence_items.summary: Background: Engagement is treated as the therapeutic dose of digital mental health interventions (DMHIs), and AI features now raise use by design. If engagement–outcome correlations reflect a dose–response, raising engagement should raise benefit by a predictable amount. This has not been tested. Methods: We reanalysed 20 historical engagement–outcome correlations (random-effects REML, prediction intervals), benchmarked them against metric-specific contemporary estimates, and updated the evidence to September 3, 2026 using a six-level engagement taxonomy. For randomised trials in which AI features increased engagement, we compared the benefit predicted by the correlations, read causally, with the observed randomised contrast, propagating uncertainty by Monte Carlo simulation. Results: The historical association was r = .249 (95% CI .171–.324; prediction interval −.052 to .508); contemporary app evidence was smaller ( r = .16). In a 540-participant trial, an AI app raised minutes of use by 0.77 SD, predicting d = 0.13 (95% uncertainty interval 0.01–0.24); observed benefit was d = −0.08 (95% CI −0.24 to 0.07). Across two trials, observed benefit fell short of prediction by d = −0.10 (95% CI −0.20 to −0.01), attenuating to −0.08 (−0.18 to 0.01) after correction for baseline imbalance. A benefit of d = 0.20 would require a 0.8–1.7 SD rise in engagement. Conclusions: Although the test rests on two randomised trials and aggregate data, engagement–outcome correlations should not be read as a dose–response: raising use did not deliver the benefit they imply. Digital mental health interventions should be optimised for therapeutic exposure rather than activity, and trials of engagement features should state, and be powered to detect, the clinical benefit their engagement gain implies.
evidence_items.title: Engagement Gains Do Not Explain Benefit: A Predicted-Versus-Observed Synthesis of Randomised Engagement-Manipulation Trials in Digital Mental Health

evidence_items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for product classification in trade compliance and supply-chain analytics. Their potential for Harmonized System (HS) classification is substantial, especially for automating six-digit code assignment over industrial records. One persistent challenge is input sparsity: enterprise systems often expose terse descriptions, abbreviated bill-of-material entries, or bare part numbers, forcing models to recover product identity before classification. Existing HS datasets rely on richer customs rulings, shipment descriptions, or synthetic product text, and cannot isolate this operational regime. To this end, we propose SemiHS-Bench, a benchmark for HS6 classification of semiconductor supply-chain products from real ERP-style text. Specifically, each product is represented through controlled input tiers derived from the same observation, with labels grounded in a held-out multilingual corpus of customs rulings. We evaluate LLM baselines on constrained and open classification, showing substantial degradation under sparse inputs. The benchmark, ruling corpus, and evaluation tools are available online at https://github.com/cti-iel/SemiHS-Bench.
evidence_items.title: SemiHS-Bench: A Semiconductor Benchmark for HS6 Classification from Sparse ERP-Style Text

rationale: Matched: agentic~evaluation, benchmark, evaluat, red teaming
evidence_items.summary: Agentic AI systems are moving from prototype demonstrations into operational workflows, yet test and evaluation (T&E) methods have not been defined to keep pace with this latest class of AI capabilities. Unlike stand-alone predictive or generative AI models, agentic systems plan multi-step work, execute actions, call tools, communicate with external services, maintain state, and hand tasks to other agents or humans. These capabilities make agentic systems useful in enterprise workflows, cyber operations, digital engineering, and decision-support settings, but they also make them harder to test and evaluate. This paper argues that T&E of agentic AI systems must move beyond model scoring to system-level assurance to establish operational confidence that a deployed agent will stay within its authority, recover from tool failures, preserve context correctly, reverse any harm it has caused, and leave enough evidence for a human to reconstruct what happened. We present a four-perspective framework for evaluating agentic AI systems: a systems perspective that defines the full system under test; a functional perspective that characterizes the degree of autonomy, authority, and workflow self-determination a system has within its operating environment; a risk perspective that addresses emergent multi-agent failure modes; and a measurement perspective that identifies technical, human-centered, temporal, and contextual metrics. We also outline a practical testing toolkit based on simulation, observational data, benchmarking, red teaming, and post-deployment monitoring.
evidence_items.title: Toward System-Level Test and Evaluation of Agentic AI Systems: Assurance, Measurement, and Bounded Trust

rationale: Matched: benchmark, dataset, evaluat, training data
evidence_items.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) have significantly advanced automatic code generation in mainstream, high-resource, general-purpose programming languages. These models are trained on large instruction-code datasets with executable test environments, which can benchmark the performance of the outputs. However, they typically underperform on low-resource, proprietary Domain Specific Langauges (DSLs) due to limited training data. In this work, we introduce a fully automated, two-stage training pipeline for adapting coding LLMs to low-resource and proprietary DSL scenarios. Stage~1 performs supervised fine-tuning (SFT) using multi granular instructions synthesized directly from raw code and comments. Stage~2 conducts Reinforcement Learning with AI Feedback (RLAIF) by generating new instructions, and subsequently Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) by choosing a preferred output. We evaluate our approach using parser success, similarity and fidelity metrics, complemented with walkthrough studies. Our results suggest that this fully automated, two-stage pipeline can enable effective adaptation of LLMs to low-resource and proprietary DSL settings under realistic data and evaluation constraints.
evidence_items.title: Adapting Code LLMs to Domain-specific Languages via Synthethic Instruction Generation and Reinforcement Learning with AI Feedback in Low-resource Settings

evidence_items.summary: Realizing large-scale quantum advantage is expected to require quantum error correction (QEC), making the compilation and optimization of logical operations a critical area of research. Logical computation imposes distinct constraints and operational paradigms that differ from those of the Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) regime, motivating the continued evolution of compilation tools. Given the complexity of this emerging stack, where factors such as gate decomposition precision and computational models must be co-designed, standardized benchmarks and toolkits are valuable for evaluating progress. To support this need, we introduce FTCircuitBench, which serves as: (1) a benchmark suite of impactful quantum algorithms, featuring pre-compiled instances in both Clifford+T and Pauli Based Computation models; (2) a modular end-to-end pipeline allowing users to compile and decompose algorithms for various fault-tolerant architectures, supporting both prebuilt and custom optimization passes; and (3) a toolkit for evaluating the impact of algorithms and optimization across the full compilation stack, providing detailed numerical analysis at each stage. FTCircuitBench is fully open-sourced and maintained on GitHub.
evidence_items.title: FTCircuitBench: A Benchmark Suite for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Compilation and Architecture
